review.imagery: Fifteen own-project renders were visually reviewed. Ten native brochure scenes and five distinct current-gallery views cover both towers, facade, pools, garden, golf practice, sunken lounge, lobby, home interiors and gym. Generic water/people images, a repeated bedroom crop and the sky-heavy distant tower resource are excluded. The full twin-tower view supplies the card and hero with a lower focal position. Proposed fitout and views remain unit-unspecific.
review.floorPlans: Four complete home drawings come from the official brochure. Seven building sheets come from a Mitchell’s Commercial Realty mirror of the SAMANA-branded floorplate pack. Exact typical-floor groups, the floor-11 equipment space and rooftop homes remain visible. Numerical unit areas and approved home-to-unit matching are absent. Confirm the selected unit and contractual area with SAMANA. All four official home sheets on physical pages 26–29 and all seven mirror floorplates on pages 2–8 were visually reviewed. The non-contiguous floor groups are transcribed exactly. No unit area is inferred, and the brochure’s three-bedroom layout remains distinct from the rooftop overview.
review.location: Complete physical page 9, including its small original regional map and all thirteen travel entries, was visually reviewed. Wider Al Barari wording is distinguished from the primary Majan project identity. The official name-only map query is saved with source hash. No coordinate, live route, road distance or operating school claim is invented.
review.provenance: Primary HTML, the original official brochure and native image origins retain source receipts and hashes. The supplementary plan pack is clearly labeled as a broker-hosted mirror. Original bytes, full sheets and physical PDF links remain available. Protected ownership and completed text research remain intact.

unavailable: Numerical drawing-specific unit areas, approved home-to-unit mapping, final fitout, verified visitor entrance coordinates, current operating status of source-era schools and dated construction photographs were not established.
